digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler / inbound probe dispatch chain
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer: differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only emits when local_state carries jira_key, but run_differs passes fetched snapshots whose entries never carry jira_key, leaving the entire downstream chain dead in production

The deletion-vs-aged-out discrimination ADR 0028 relies on is already implemented twice via outbound_differ._safe_get_issue and binding_walk bounded GETs, both live and verified on DC; the inbound probe arm is architecturally redundant

When a binding is retired after 3 confirmed 404s, _retire pops it from both bindings and reverse, making the local ticket unbound, and outbound_differ then creates a fresh Jira issue—the same-pass resurrection c244 promised is inert but eventual resurrection exists on a 3-pass delay
Prior art (Unito, Kubernetes) rejects resurrection: once deleted in Jira, a work item should not be resurrected; the operator ruling settles this by tombstoning confirmed-deleted pairings

A guard must prevent outbound CREATE for local tickets whose binding was retired on confirmed 404, while never-bound local tickets still create normally, made observable via bridge alert naming the retired key and BindingStore.unretire as the reversal route

The dead legacy chain (producer, dispatch arm, route_inbound_probe, fixture-only test, and same-pass resurrection implementation) is removed; the port capability (probe_remote, SupportsAbsenceProbe, inbound_probe.py) is retained as dormant pending epic e369 AC5 review
